To the best of our knowledge, the new discovery that quantum codes are simultaneously optimal pure quantum $(r,δ)$-LRCs and record-breaking quantum codes has not been previously reported in the literature.

AI.tldr: The paper presents advancements in quantum codes using $τ$-optimal defining matrices (τ-OD), establishing a unified theorem and discovering new infinite families of such matrices, leading to 222 record-breaking quantum codes and 30 optimal pure quantum $(r,δ)$-LRCs.
AI.motivation: To develop new quantum codes and $(r,δ)$-LRCs through the application of MP codes with $τ$-OD matrices, expanding the theoretical groundwork and practical implementations.
AI.method: A unified $τ$-monomial decomposition theorem for self-adjoint matrices over finite fields was established, leading to the discovery of infinite families of $τ$-OD matrices; MP codes were used to construct quantum codes and $(r,δ)$-LRCs.
AI.result: The paper reports 222 new quantum codes that break existing records and introduces 30 optimal pure quantum $(r,δ)$-LRCs, some of which are simultaneously record-breaking.
AI.conclusion: This work extends existing knowledge on quantum codes, revealing that certain codes can achieve optimality and record-breaking status together, a previously unreported phenomenon.

title: High-scale Mirror Standard Model Dark Matter, Dark Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves Implications
summary: We consider a scenario for dark matter in the Universe, according to which the dark matter sector is comprised by a dark Standard Model sector which interacts only gravitationally with the ordinary Standard Model sector. This dark Standard Model sector is assumed to have the same symmetries as the ordinary Standard Model, with the couplings and the scale of the mirror Standard Model sector being different than the ordinary Standard Model sector. Specifically, the scale of the mirror Standard Model sector will be assumed to be quite higher compared to the ordinary Standard Model. Also the Yukawa couplings among the mirror Higgs and the mirror fermions are assumed to be different from those of the Standard Model and we examine the effects of the different scale and of the different Yukawas on the evolution of the Universe. As we show, a mirror world phase transition occurs at high temperatures of the baryonic Universe, which can be first order or second order, depending on the scale of the Universe and the Yukawa couplings. These are dark phase transitions which occur quite earlier than the real world Standard Model electroweak phase transition. The case of a second order phase transition is quite interesting phenomenologically, since it can potentially have a direct imprint on the spectrum of stochastic gravitational waves for frequencies probed by the future gravitational wave detectors. Also we examine whether this mirror dark matter world can form atoms and as we show in some scenario the high scale mirror dark matter can have both atomic and subatomic particle components. We also give an approximation of the total equation of state of high scale mirror DM and we discuss how high scale mirror DM can reconcile contradicting observations like the Bullet cluster and the Abell 520 cluster.

AI.tldr: The paper explores a dark Standard Model sector interacting only via gravity with the ordinary Standard Model. It discusses the implications of differing scales and Yukawa couplings on the Universe's evolution, highlighting dark phase transitions and their potential effects on gravitational waves. The findings suggest that high scale mirror dark matter could form atomic structures and address inconsistencies in astrophysical observations.
AI.motivation: To examine the properties and implications of a gravitationally interacting dark Standard Model sector, particularly how it could resolve existing astrophysical inconsistencies.
AI.method: Analysis of a dark Standard Model sector with differing scales and Yukawa couplings, study of phase transitions and their effects on gravitational wave spectra, and assessment of mirror dark matter's atomic formation.
AI.result: Identified possible first or second order phase transitions in the dark sector, which could influence gravitational wave observations. Also demonstrated conditions under which mirror dark matter can form atomic structures.
AI.conclusion: High scale mirror dark matter can reconcile observed phenomena like the Bullet and Abell 520 clusters while exhibiting interesting characteristics such as potential atomic formation.

title: Pulse profile modelling of accreting millisecond pulsars with disc occultation and its impact on parameter inference
comment: 16 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to MNRAS
summary: Pulse profile modelling is a relativistic ray-tracing technique used to infer neutron star mass, radius, and surface hotspot properties from X-ray pulsations. Pulse profile modelling has been widely applied to rotation-powered millisecond pulsars, where the local environment is relatively empty. Application to accreting millisecond pulsars is complicated by the geometry of the local accretion flow, including disc occultation of surface emission. In this work, we extend an established pulse profile modelling code, X-PSI, to incorporate accretion disc occultation in accreting millisecond pulsar pulse profile modelling. We quantify how disc occultation depends on system geometry and evaluate its impact on parameter inference. We find that disc occultation is primarily governed by the viewing inclination and can significantly reshape pulse profiles at moderate to high inclinations. Using synthetic Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer datasets, we investigate parameter recovery for two representative hotspot configurations. For hotspots close to the rotational poles, statistically acceptable fits can yield posteriors that deviate noticeably from the true parameters. In contrast, in a case with hotspots located closer to the equator we find more reliable parameter recovery. We further find that neglecting disc occultation can introduce spurious posterior modes with comparable statistical support, potentially affecting the interpretation of inferred neutron star parameters, suggesting that this effect should be included in accreting millisecond pulsar pulse profile modelling.

AI.tldr: This study enhances pulse profile modelling for accreting millisecond pulsars by integrating accretion disc occultation effects, revealing its critical role in parameter inference accuracy.
AI.motivation: To improve the accuracy of neutron star parameter inference by considering the effects of accretion disc geometry in pulse profile modelling.
AI.method: Extending the X-PSI code to include disc occultation effects, quantifying its impacts on pulse profiles through simulations of various hotspot configurations.
AI.result: Disc occultation primarily affects profiles based on viewing inclination, with hotspots near the poles leading to significant deviations in inferred parameters compared to those closer to the equator.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating disc occultation is essential for accurate inference of neutron star properties in accreting millisecond pulsars, as neglecting it may lead to misleading results.

title: Dose-efficient Quantum Phase Estimation in Lossy Optical Interferometry
summary: Optical interferometry is a cornerstone technique for precise phase measurements across various fields. In many applications, for example, biological imaging, it often necessitates stringent limits on light intensity to prevent adverse effects on light-sensitive samples, a condition known as dose-limited regimes. Maximizing the precision per dose is therefore crucial. In quantum metrology, quantum correlations enable high precision in phase estimation while adhering to dose constraints. Nevertheless, photon loss, including absorption by a sample, substantially diminishes the benefits of quantum enhancement in interferometry. In this work, we experimentally investigate a dose-efficient approach to quantum phase estimation using sequential strategies in the presence of loss. Performance of sequential strategies with and without control is evaluated through quantum Fisher information (QFI) per dose. Experimental results show that both sequential strategies exceed the classical limit and outperform the parallel strategy using unbalanced N00N states. Notably, the control-enhanced sequential strategy attains superior QFI per dose, approaching the quantum limit. These results highlight the promise of sequential strategy for imaging and sensing in resource-constrained scenarios, marking a significant step toward practical and efficient quantum metrology in lossy environments.

AI.tldr: This study presents an experimental approach to enhance quantum phase estimation in optical interferometry under dose-limited regimes, demonstrating that sequential strategies outperform traditional methods amid photon loss.
AI.motivation: The need to maximize precision in optical interferometry, particularly under light intensity constraints to protect sensitive samples, motivates this research.
AI.method: The authors utilized sequential phase estimation strategies and evaluated their performance using quantum Fisher information (QFI) per dose, comparing results from controlled and uncontrolled scenarios.
AI.result: Experimental findings indicate that both sequential strategies surpass classical limits and outperform parallel strategies, with the control-enhanced sequential strategy achieving near-quantum limit performance.
AI.conclusion: This research underscores the potential of sequential strategies for advancing practical quantum metrology, particularly in situations characterized by resource limitations and photon loss.

title: Bose-enhanced Neutrino Decays in a Thermal Medium
summary: We compute the decay width of neutrinos in a thermal medium using finite-temperature quantum field theory, focusing on non-standard decays into lighter neutrinos and a scalar or light vector boson. We derive general expressions for the thermal decay rate and show that finite-temperature effects can dramatically enhance neutrino decays when the parent and daughter states are nearly degenerate in mass. In this regime, the emitted boson is kinematically soft and undergoes strong Bose enhancement, leading to decay widths that can exceed their vacuum values by a couple of orders of magnitude. We demonstrate that this effect is largely insensitive to the Lorentz structure of the underlying interaction and arises generically from the interplay of thermal occupation factors and quasi-degenerate kinematics. Our results highlight a previously underappreciated feature of neutrino decay in thermal environments and provide a general framework applicable to a broad class of fermionic decay processes.

AI.tldr: The study calculates the thermal decay width of neutrinos in a medium, revealing that near-degenerate mass states significantly enhance decay rates due to thermal effects.
AI.motivation: To explore how thermal environments affect neutrino decay processes, particularly for non-standard decays into lighter neutrinos and bosons.
AI.method: Utilizing finite-temperature quantum field theory to derive decay rate expressions and analyzing effects of thermal occupation and kinematics.
AI.result: Demonstrated significant enhancement of decay widths in thermal conditions, particularly for nearly degenerate mass states, with results largely independent of interaction specifics.
AI.conclusion: The findings present a new understanding of neutrino decay in thermal environments, offering a framework for various fermionic decays.

title: Spectral Softenings, Composition Bump, and Anisotropy Transition: A Consistent Picture of Cosmic-Ray Origin Below the Knee
summary: Recent DAMPE measurements of individual cosmic-ray components, including carbon, oxygen, and iron, reveal distinct spectral softenings below the knee. The energy spectrum, mass composition, and anisotropy together provide key probes of cosmic-ray origin and propagation. By incorporating the individual elemental spectra reported by DAMPE, we derive a more complete $\langle \ln A\rangle$ distribution, which smoothly connects to the higher-energy $\langle \ln A\rangle$ measurements from LHAASO and exhibits a pronounced bump-like feature. This feature indicates a transition from the conventional Galactic cosmic ray source population to a nearby-source-dominated regime. We show that a spatially dependent propagation model with a nearby-source contribution can consistently reproduce the observed spectra, mass composition, and anisotropy. This suggests a unified picture in which Galactic cosmic rays below the knee arise from multiple source populations jointly constrained by these observables. Leveraging the precise component-resolved spectra from DAMPE, we further predict the transition energies in the anisotropy phase and amplitude for different mass components. Future component-resolved anisotropy measurements by LHAASO will provide a crucial test of this scenario.

AI.tldr: DAMPE's measurements reveal distinct features in cosmic rays' energy spectra, indicating multiple source contributions and a transition in cosmic-ray origin.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin and propagation of cosmic rays through detailed analysis of individual cosmic-ray components.
AI.method: Analyzed individual elemental spectra from DAMPE to derive a comprehensive mass composition distribution and employed a spatially dependent propagation model incorporating nearby sources.
AI.result: A pronounced bump in the mass distribution indicates a transition from standard Galactic sources to nearby sources; the model effectively reproduces observed cosmic-ray characteristics.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that Galactic cosmic rays below the knee stem from diverse source populations, and future anisotropy measurements will validate this model.

title: A new class of degenerate solutions to the massless Dirac equation and their potential applications in optical memories
summary: In this article, we present a novel class of degenerate solutions to the massless Dirac equation, corresponding to a wide variety of electromagnetic 4-potentials and fields, including both zero field and circularly polarized electromagnetic waves. An interesting property of these solutions is that the spin of the particles rotates in synchronization with the electric and magnetic fields of the electromagnetic waves. These results could be utilized for the development of optical memories based on materials supporting massless Dirac fermions, such as graphene.

AI.tldr: The article introduces novel degenerate solutions to the massless Dirac equation with applications to electromagnetic fields, highlighting synchronized spin rotation with field configurations.
AI.motivation: To explore new solutions to the massless Dirac equation that can be applied to various electromagnetic contexts and potentially enhance optical memory technologies.
AI.method: By analyzing the massless Dirac equation under different electromagnetic 4-potentials, the authors derive degenerate solutions and examine their properties.
AI.result: The study reveals that the spin of particles aligns and rotates with the electromagnetic fields, including both static and dynamic configurations.
AI.conclusion: These findings have implications for developing advanced optical memories utilizing materials like graphene that support massless Dirac fermions.

title: Light hybrid baryons in the constituent model of QCD
summary: Hybrid baryons, in which gluonic degrees of freedom play an explicit dynamical role, provide a key testing ground for nonperturbative quantum chromodynamics. In this work, we investigate the mass spectrum of light hybrid baryons composed of identical quarks within a phenomenological constituent framework, applied to a quark core-gluon approximation. In this approach, the hybrid baryon is described as a bound state of a color-octet three-quark core and a constituent gluon, allowing the original four-body problem to be reduced to a three-body calculation followed by an effective two-body treatment. The spectrum of the color-octet quark core is obtained by solving a semirelativistic three-quark Hamiltonian with linear confinement, Coulomb, and regularized hyperfine interactions using an oscillator basis expansion. Finite-size effects of the core are incorporated through the convolution of the effective core-gluon interaction with the spatial quark density. The resulting two-body problem, whose associated Hamiltonian has the same shape as the one of the core, is solved applying the helicity formalism and using the Lagrange mesh method. Our results predict the lightest hybrid baryons to occur at energies above $3~\mathrm{GeV}$, with negative-parity states generally lying below their positive-parity counterparts. The predicted spectra are compared with lattice QCD and QCD sum-rule calculations, showing qualitative agreement although the lowest-lying lattice QCD results are significantly lighter than the present ones. Possible extensions of the model and implications for future experimental searches are discussed.

AI.tldr: This study investigates the mass spectrum of light hybrid baryons using a constituent framework, demonstrating their properties and relationship with quantum chromodynamics.
AI.motivation: To explore the dynamics of hybrid baryons, which are crucial for understanding nonperturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD).
AI.method: The mass spectrum is analyzed using a quark core-gluon approximation, reducing a four-body problem into manageable calculations involving a three-body core and a two-body treatment, utilizing semirelativistic Hamiltonians and helicity formalism.
AI.result: The analysis predicts that light hybrid baryons exist at energies above 3 GeV, with negative-parity states generally found to be lighter than positive-parity ones, aligning qualitatively with lattice QCD results despite some discrepancies in absolute mass values.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide new insights into hybrid baryon properties, emphasizing the need for future experimental validation and potential model extensions.

title: Linear Gravitational Wave Memory Through the Window of Core-Collapse Supernovae
summary: Low-frequency gravitational waves ($\lessapprox$ 50 Hz) from core-collapse supernovae are becoming more important for current and future gravitational wave studies. This frequency region is dominated by the global morphology of the explosion and the anisotropic emission of neutrinos from the event. This paper serves as a brief review of both theory and detection (prospects) for gravitational waves in the low-frequency region. We discuss the generation of the linear gravitational wave memory sourced from neutrino emission and show results from an example 15 $M_{\odot}$ Solar metallicity progenitor. We also discuss the detection of the linear gravitational wave memory in current detectors, utilizing a combination of a linear predictive filter and matched templating. Finally we will discuss detection prospects in future detectors such as Cosmic Explorer, Einstein Telescope, the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, and the Lunar Gravitational-wave Antenna.

AI.tldr: The paper reviews low-frequency gravitational waves from core-collapse supernovae, focusing on their generation, detection approaches, and future detection prospects.
AI.motivation: Investigating low-frequency gravitational waves is essential for understanding core-collapse supernovae and improving detection methods in gravitational wave astronomy.
AI.method: The paper reviews theory and detection techniques, including linear gravitational wave memory from neutrino emission, and utilizes linear predictive filtering and matched templating for detection analysis.
AI.result: The paper presents results from an example 15 $M_{\odot}$ progenitor and evaluates detection capabilities in current and future gravitational wave detectors.
AI.conclusion: Future detectors like Cosmic Explorer and Einstein Telescope may enhance the detection of low-frequency gravitational waves, expanding our understanding of core-collapse supernovae.

title: Quantum-Classical Hierarchical Equations of Motion
summary: We develop a quantum-classical hierarchical equations of motion (QC-HEOM) approach for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems. The method combines the ensemble-averaged classical path reference of the quantum-classical path integral formalism with a hierarchy of auxiliary quantum influence functionals. By incorporating thermal fluctuations through an ensemble average over reference trajectories, the hierarchy is required to represent only the residual quantum memory associated with the imaginary part of the bath response function. Consequently, unlike conventional hierarchical equations of motion, QC-HEOM does not require Matsubara or Padé expansions of the thermal kernel and exhibits only weak temperature dependence of the hierarchy size. Furthermore, because thermal fluctuations are supplied through reference classical trajectories, the framework naturally extends beyond harmonic baths and enables the incorporation of anharmonic and molecular environments through externally generated trajectories. We derive the formalism and demonstrate its exactness for a harmonic bath. Applications to an asymmetric spin-boson model and the seven-site Fenna--Matthews--Olson complex illustrate the accuracy of QC-HEOM. It reproduces benchmark quasi-adiabatic path integral and hierarchical equations of motion results while requiring substantially fewer auxiliary objects, particularly at low temperatures. These results establish QC-HEOM as an efficient framework for treating residual quantum memory in quantum-classical descriptions of open-system dynamics. The separation of thermal fluctuations from residual quantum memory through the use of Wigner trajectories provides an approximate route toward hierarchical treatments of complex anharmonic environments that are inaccessible to conventional HEOM approaches.

AI.tldr: The QC-HEOM method efficiently simulates non-Markovian open quantum systems by utilizing classical paths and a hierarchy of quantum influence functionals, reducing complexity and enhancing accuracy compared to traditional methods.
AI.motivation: To improve simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems by addressing limitations in conventional hierarchical equations of motion.
AI.method: The QC-HEOM approach combines ensemble-averaged classical paths with a hierarchy of quantum influence functionals, allowing for the incorporation of thermal fluctuations and reducing dependency on complex expansions.
AI.result: QC-HEOM shows improved accuracy and efficiency, particularly at low temperatures, reproducing results similar to benchmark methods while requiring fewer auxiliary objects.
AI.conclusion: QC-HEOM is an efficient framework for modeling residual quantum memory in open-system dynamics, extending capabilities to complex anharmonic environments.

title: Tripartite entanglement of oscillating and decohering neutrinos
summary: We study entanglement measures for oscillating neutrinos in the wave-packet formalism and confirm that an oscillating neutrino exhibits genuine tripartite entanglement and can be characterized as a member of the W class of states. We also show that this feature survives in the decoherence limit, and discuss the effect of CP phases on the entanglement. These findings provide new insights into the quantum nature of neutrino oscillations and their potential role in quantum information science, especially for neutrinos propagating large distances such as the astrophysical neutrinos observed at neutrino telescopes.

AI.tldr: A study establishes entanglement measures for oscillating neutrinos, identifying genuine tripartite entanglement and its persistence under decoherence, along with the impact of CP phases.
AI.motivation: Investigating the quantum properties of neutrinos may enhance understanding of neutrino oscillations and their application in quantum information science.
AI.method: Utilizing the wave-packet formalism, the study analyzes tripartite entanglement in oscillating neutrinos and evaluates the effects of decoherence and CP phases.
AI.result: Oscillating neutrinos exhibit genuine tripartite entanglement and align with the W class of states, maintaining these characteristics despite decoherence.
AI.conclusion: The research advances knowledge in quantum neutrino behavior and suggests implications for quantum information technologies, particularly with astrophysical neutrinos observed in telescopes.

title: Cosmological signals of dark matter semi-annihilation
summary: The growth of primordial density fluctuations in the early Universe leads to an inhomogeneous dark matter distribution at high redshift, where semi-annihilation processes of the form $χχ\rightarrow χ^c ν$ can occur with a sizable rate. Using a state-of-the-art model for the cosmological boost factor, we compute the resulting redshift-dependent flux of boosted dark matter particles generated by semi-annihilation, and we study the implications of the boosted component for structure formation and direct detection experiments. We find that the cosmological contribution can enhance the sensitivity of current dark matter searches by up to three orders of magnitude, and may allow future experiments to probe scattering cross sections in the femtobarn range for dark matter masses between $\sim 10$ MeV and $\sim1$ GeV.

AI.tldr: Research on dark matter reveals that semi-annihilation processes significantly enhance detection sensitivity, allowing exploration of lower mass ranges in future experiments.
AI.motivation: To understand how primordial density fluctuations impact dark matter distribution and detection methods in the early Universe.
AI.method: The study employs a cosmological boost factor model to compute the redshift-dependent flux of dark matter particles resulting from semi-annihilation processes.
AI.result: Findings indicate that the semi-annihilation processes can boost dark matter detection sensitivity by up to three orders of magnitude, enabling the probing of lower mass regimes.
AI.conclusion: The enhanced sensitivity may allow future experiments to detect dark matter scattering cross sections in the femtobarn range for masses from approximately 10 MeV to 1 GeV.

title: Quantum sensing through bosonic-fermionic Bell-state transitions in two-photon interference
summary: Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference has become a central resource for quantum sensing and metrology owing to its sensitivity to temporal delay and photon indistinguishability. However, existing HOM-based sensing schemes generally rely on inserting a sample into one arm of the interferometer, making the measurement vulnerable to optical loss, alignment instability, and bandwidth-dependent distortion of the interference profile. Here, we demonstrate a symmetry-controlled quantum sensing scheme based on continuous transitions between symmetric (bosonic-like) and antisymmetric (fermionic-like) Bell states in two-photon interference. By imprinting a geometric phase onto the classical pump beam and transferring it to polarization-entangled photons generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion, we coherently tune the exchange symmetry of the entangled state without altering the temporal or spectral indistinguishability of the photons. The HOM response evolves continuously from bunching to antibunching with a sine square phase dependence, producing a coincidence modulation of approximately 10 * 10^4 counts s^-1 counts/s. In contrast to conventional HOM sensing, the phase-modulation linewidth remains fixed at pi/2, independent of photon bandwidth. Using a birefringent crystal placed directly in the pump beam, we measure thermo-dispersive birefringence with a resolution of the order of 10^{-6} over a broad temperature range. Our results establish exchange symmetry as a controllable resource for robust quantum sensing and symmetry-engineered photonic quantum information processing.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a new quantum sensing scheme utilizing symmetry-controlled transitions between Bell states to enhance sensitivity and stability against conventional measurement issues.
AI.motivation: Existing HOM-based sensing faces limitations from optical loss and alignment instability, hindering robust measurements.
AI.method: The proposed scheme uses geometric phase imprinting on a pump beam to continuously modulate the exchange symmetry of polarization-entangled photons, allowing control over the quantum interference response without sacrificing photon indistinguishability.
AI.result: The HOM response exhibits a continuous shift from bunching to antibunching with a stable modulation rate of ~10 * 10^4 counts/s and a fixed phase-modulation linewidth of pi/2, regardless of bandwidth.
AI.conclusion: The findings demonstrate that exchange symmetry can be precisely controlled for enhanced robustness in quantum sensing applications, suggesting its potential for advancing quantum information processing.

title: Efficient calculation of exclusive diffractive cross sections at the EIC and LHeC with the Sartre event generator
summary: We present a new version of the Sartre event generator for exclusive diffraction at small xP in the colour dipole model, for $ep$ and $e$A scattering at the EIC and the LHeC as well as ultra-peripheral $pp$, $p$A, and AA collisions at RHIC and the LHC. Sartre stores the first and second moment of the interaction amplitudes in lookup tables which are then used for efficient event generation. There are many possible combinations of processes in Sartre, with different initial state nuclear targets and different final state vector mesons or real photons. We also want to implement different versions of the dipole model: with and without non-linear saturation effects, with and without nucleon hotspot substructure. A long-standing bottleneck for simulating all possible exclusive processes has been the production of lookup tables, which take a few CPU-year for each combination, necessitating the use of computing farms. The calculation also involves integrations of rapidly fluctuating integrands, which may cause numerical glitches which takes much effort to smoothen out. In this paper we present a solution to these issues, by presenting a new numerical calculation which improves the efficiency in the table production by 3-4 orders of magnitudes. This enables us to produce lookup tables for any process that we may be interested in, in a few hours. The new calculation does also not exhibit numerical glitches. We provide novel predictions for the EIC and the LHeC using the new version of Sartre.

AI.tldr: This paper describes an upgraded version of the Sartre event generator for simulating exclusive diffraction processes, improving efficiency in generating lookup tables and resolving numerical issues.
AI.motivation: The aim is to enhance the simulation of exclusive diffraction in various scattering scenarios, addressing previous inefficiencies and numerical glitches in the process of generating lookup tables.
AI.method: The paper introduces a new numerical approach that significantly streamlines the production of lookup tables for interaction amplitudes in the Sartre generator, achieving a speedup of 3-4 orders of magnitude.
AI.result: The new method allows for efficient table production for different nuclear targets and final state outputs, completed within hours rather than years, while eliminating previous numerical glitches.
AI.conclusion: This advancement enables comprehensive simulations of exclusive diffraction processes at EIC and LHeC, offering new predictions and simplifying the research process.

title: Jones-matrix analysis of phase accumulation in a linear-optical multi-pass interferometer
summary: Quantum information science has traditionally relied on nonclassical resources, such as entangled photon pairs and squeezed states, to achieve measurement performance beyond classical limits. Here, we revisit the multi-pass photonic scheme reported in Nature 450, 393 (2007) to clarify the physical origin of the observed superresolution and the associated claim of supersensitivity. Using a rigorous Jones-matrix formalism, we show that the round-trip evolution of the HQMQ linear optics unit is equivalent to the product of two reflections in polarization space, resulting in an effective rotation operator. This equivalence reveals that the accumulated phase arises from coherent polarization-state rotation on the Poincare'e sphere. The resulting phase accumulation is interpreted geometrically as a progressive realignment of the polarization state during successive forward and backward propagations. To validate the theoretical model, a classical-wave implementation is experimentally conducted, analyzed, and compared with the corresponding Jones-matrix solution. Finally, the scaling behavior of the Fisher information is analyzed to examine the origin of the claimed supersensitivity. The results are further compared with a recently developed coherence de Broglie wavelength framework, which achieves identical superresolution through repeated coherent interactions in a cascaded interferometeric architecture.

AI.tldr: This study reexamines a multi-pass photonic scheme for superresolution and supersensitivity in quantum measurements using a Jones-matrix formalism to demonstrate phase accumulation via polarization rotation.
AI.motivation: To clarify mechanisms behind superresolution and supersensitivity in quantum information science using classical and nonclassical resources.
AI.method: Employing a rigorous Jones-matrix approach to model the round-trip evolution of the optics unit, demonstrating phase accumulation through coherent polarization-state rotation on the Poincaré sphere, and validating with classical-wave experiments.
AI.result: Findings reveal a geometric interpretation of phase accumulation through polarization state realignment, and the analysis of Fisher information confirms the origin of supersensitivity.
AI.conclusion: The study links classical-wave implementations to quantum phenomena, comparing results with a coherence de Broglie wavelength framework that achieves similar superresolution via cascaded interactions.

title: Spin counting via projection noise measurement of mesoscopic solid-state spin ensemble
summary: Quantum projection noise is the fundamental noise source for the population measurement of spin ensembles. While projection-noise-limited measurements have been extensively studied in atomic systems, corresponding experiments on solid-state spin ensembles remain challenging due to dominant classical readout noise. Here, we report direct measurement of the quantum projection noise of mesoscopic ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spin defects at room temperature. Our experiment is enabled by a high optically-detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast of over 20% for a single crystallographic orientation of the defect spins, obtained by combining polarization-selective optical excitation with spin-to-charge conversion. We use our protocol to demonstrate projection noise measurements and spin counting from nanoscale NV ensembles of up to 43 spins. We further demonstrate that the protocol allows for significant gains in sensitivity for magnetometry applications without need for cryogenic operation or high bias magnetic fields.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a novel method for measuring quantum projection noise in mesoscopic ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spin defects at room temperature, enabling improved magnetometry sensitivity.
AI.motivation: The study addresses the challenge of measuring quantum projection noise in solid-state spin ensembles, where classical noise often dominates.
AI.method: The authors achieved high ODMR contrast using polarization-selective optical excitation and spin-to-charge conversion to measure projection noise and perform spin counting in NV ensembles of up to 43 spins.
AI.result: The method demonstrated successful measurement of quantum projection noise and significant increases in sensitivity for magnetometry applications without requiring cryogenic conditions.
AI.conclusion: This work enhances the feasibility of high-precision measurements in solid-state systems, leading to advancements in magnetometry.

title: In search for signals of the $D\bar{D}$ bound state $X(3700)$ from study of the $B^+ \to D^+ D^- K^+$, $B^0 \to D^+ D^- K^0$ and $Λ_b \to D^+ D^- Λ$ reactions
summary: We perform a theoretical study of the $B^+ \to D^+ D^- K^+$, $B^0 \to D^+ D^- K^0$ and $Λ_b \to D^+ D^- Λ$ reactions by looking at the production mechanisms, with special emphasis in the final state interaction of the charmed mesons, which gives rise to the $X_{c0}(3930)$, coupling strongly to $D_s\bar{D}_s$, and another state that we call $X(3700)$, coupling strongly to $D \bar D$ that qualifies as a $D \bar D$ bound state. The combined study of all these reactions shows that the final state interaction responsible for the production of these resonances is more important in the $B^+ \to D^+ D^- K^+$ reaction than in the $Λ_b \to D^+ D^- Λ$ one. We have taken this into account and shown that normalizing the $D^+ D^-$ mass distributions to the same value at the peak of the $ψ(3770)$ production, the two mass distributions are quite different in a range of 10 MeV above the $D^+ D^-$ threshold, with a value about 13 times bigger for the $B^+ \to D^+ D^- K^+$ reaction than for the $Λ_b \to D^+ D^- Λ$ one. We make a call to measure these magnitudes in the coming LHCb upgrades, which would bring great support to the existence of the bound $D^+ D^-$ state.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the reactions $B^+ 	o D^+ D^- K^+$, $B^0 	o D^+ D^- K^0$, and $Λ_b 	o D^+ D^- Λ$, focusing on the final state interactions of charmed mesons that generate resonances like $X_{c0}(3930)$ and a bound state $X(3700)$. The research indicates a significant difference in the final state interaction strength between the $B^+$ and $Λ_b$ reactions, highlighting the importance of upcoming measurements to validate the existence of the bound state.
AI.motivation: To explore the production mechanisms of specific B-meson decay reactions and understand the dynamics of charmed meson final states, particularly resonances and bound states.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of B-meson decay mechanisms with emphasis on final state interactions, supported by comparisons of mass distributions from related reactions.
AI.result: A comparison of mass distributions reveals that the $B^+ 	o D^+ D^- K^+$ reaction has a peak approximately 13 times larger than that of the $Λ_b 	o D^+ D^- Λ$, indicating stronger final state interactions for the former.
AI.conclusion: The findings encourage further measurements at LHCb to provide evidence for the strongly coupled bound $D^+ D^-$ state.

title: Dealing with locality in QAOA
summary: Shallow-depth QAOA on sparse, high-diameter MaxCut instances faces a locality bottleneck: at depth \(p\), local observables can depend only on a bounded neighborhood of the circuit interaction graph. We propose a transport-augmented QAOA that keeps the MaxCut cost Hamiltonian unchanged but enriches the mixer with optimized, unweighted shortcut couplings (scheduled \(XX+YY\)) to collapse the effective interaction-graph diameter. Using exact finite-depth support recursions, we relate optimal shortcut placement to bounded-diameter graph augmentation, and show in benchmarks that (unlike ma-QAOA) performance becomes effectively size-invariant once the diameter is reduced. For bipartite families (base diameter 4), reducing the interaction path to \(d=1\) raises the ensemble-averaged approximation ratio from 0.7378 (ma-QAOA) to 0.9767 at \(p=1\) (\(σ=0.0251\), nine system sizes); on random trees (base diameter 10), at \(p=2\) it improves from 0.9226 to 0.9997 (\(σ=0.0001\)).

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a transport-augmented QAOA to improve performance on MaxCut problems by optimizing mixer couplings, effectively addressing locality limitations associated with circuit depth and diameter.
AI.motivation: The motivation stems from the locality bottleneck encountered in shallow-depth QAOA for sparse, high-diameter MaxCut instances, which affects performance due to limited interaction among observables.
AI.method: The method involves enhancing the mixer in the QAOA with optimized, unweighted shortcut couplings, while keeping the MaxCut cost Hamiltonian unchanged, and using finite-depth support recursions to analyze optimal coupling placements.
AI.result: Benchmarks indicate a significant performance improvement; for bipartite graphs, the approximation ratio increases from 0.7378 to 0.9767 at depth 1, and for random trees, it rises from 0.9226 to 0.9997 at depth 2, showing size-invariance after reducing diameter.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach effectively mitigates locality issues in QAOA, demonstrating enhanced performance and promising implications for other graph-based problems.

title: Leptonic flavour transfer: a new window on flavour gauge symmetries
summary: New flavour non-abelian gauge groups, which may arise as part of a fundamental theory of flavour, can lead to distinctive flavour-transfer processes. When restricted to the lepton sector, such processes partially mimic the standard charged current interactions at low energy. We explicitly study such constructions with various flavour structures, and investigate systematically all relevant accelerator-based constraints, exploring specific experimental signatures for these models. In the absence of flavour-breaking spurions, constraints from heavy lepton lifetime are found to dominate over most of the parameter space, with specific parts still open for future ee-collider searches. Numerical predictions are obtained using the \texttt{MARTY} framework, allowing us to consistently explore both the light- and heavy-mediator regimes. Finally, using \darkpack, we also assessed that extensions of such models could be compatible with dark matter relic density bounds.

AI.tldr: This paper explores new non-abelian gauge groups in the lepton sector and their potential implications for flavour-transfer processes, comparing these to standard interactions and assessing experimental constraints, particularly from heavy lepton lifetimes.
AI.motivation: To investigate new theoretical frameworks for flavour interactions and their consistency with existing experimental data, especially in the lepton sector.
AI.method: The paper employs a systematic study of various flavour structures and constraints from accelerator experiments, utilizing the MARTY framework for numerical predictions and darkpack for dark matter compatibility assessments.
AI.result: Findings reveal that heavy lepton lifetime constraints dominate most parameter space, with certain regions still viable for future searches at electron-positron colliders.
AI.conclusion: Extensions of these models are potentially compatible with dark matter relic density, suggesting further avenues for theoretical exploration and experimental verification.

title: Optimal Decoding of Small Codes by Density Matrix Propagation
summary: Accurate and efficient decoding is a crucial component for achieving fault-tolerant quantum computing. Realistic circuit-level noise introduces temporal correlations and degeneracy, making optimal (maximum-likelihood) decoding computationally intractable in general. As a result, practical decoders rely on heuristic approximations, and it is generally difficult to quantify how suboptimal they are, as this strongly depends on the code and noise model considered. In this work, we study the accuracy of practical decoding algorithms under circuit-level noise by comparing them against a maximum likelihood decoding benchmark. Our approach propagates the density matrix through the full memory experiment and computes the optimal decoding decision for each syndrome history. We introduce pruning techniques with rigorous bounds, allowing us to access larger numbers of syndrome-extraction rounds. We apply this framework to small instances of the repetition code and a cellular automaton code, and benchmark minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM), belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding (BP+OSD), Tesseract, and Planar decoders against optimal decoding. While standard decoders remain close to optimal for the repetition code, we find significant deviations for the cellular automaton code, with BP+OSD deteriorating already in experimentally relevant noise regimes. Moreover, the pruning method developed here highlights that, at low physical error rates, only a narrow fraction of syndrome histories contributes significantly to the logical error rate.

AI.tldr: This study evaluates practical quantum decoding algorithms against a maximum likelihood benchmark, highlighting significant deviations in performance depending on code and noise model.
AI.motivation: To address the challenges posed by circuit-level noise in quantum computing and assess the effectiveness of practical decoding algorithms.
AI.method: The study uses density matrix propagation to compute optimal decoding for each syndrome history, applying pruning techniques to explore more syndrome-extraction rounds.
AI.result: While standard decoders perform well for repetition codes, their performance falters for cellular automaton codes, particularly under higher noise levels, with BP+OSD showing early deterioration.
AI.conclusion: At low physical error rates, only a small subset of syndrome histories has a considerable impact on the logical error rate.

title: QCI Connect: A Modular Full-Stack Quantum Computing Platform
summary: In a world of various competing quantum computing architectures, hardware-agnostic, full-stack platforms are necessary to bring the full power of quantum computing hardware to domain experts via the cloud. QCI Connect and its Software Development Kit provide a reference architecture for a full-stack platform with a modular design and open-source interface definitions, built to facilitate a community-driven application ecosystem. Here, we present its overall design and features, central interfaces, and lessons learned, both for users of the platform and as a reference guide for future developments.

AI.tldr: QCI Connect is a hardware-agnostic, full-stack quantum computing platform designed to support domain experts through cloud access, featuring a modular architecture and open-source interfaces.
AI.motivation: As various quantum computing architectures emerge, a unified platform is needed to enable domain experts to access quantum computing resources effectively.
AI.method: QCI Connect offers a modular design and an accompanying Software Development Kit that allows for community-driven application development through open-source interface definitions.
AI.result: The paper details the platform's design, main features, and interfaces, providing insights aimed at users and informing future development efforts.
AI.conclusion: QCI Connect serves as a valuable reference for building innovative quantum computing applications while fostering a collaborative ecosystem.

title: Sensitivity of polaron-molecule observables to MDR/GUP-like ultraviolet deformations at low energies via quantum computing
summary: We show that impurity many-body observables can display enhanced sensitivity to ultraviolet deformations of generalized-uncertainty-principle and modified-dispersion-relation type at accessible energy scales. Using a deformed polaron-molecule Hamiltonian constructed to preserve the infrared sector, we quantify the impact of such deformations on spectral and Ramsey observables and implement the corresponding dynamics in a controlled quantum computing setting. We identify regimes near the polaron-molecule crossover where small ultraviolet deformations are strongly amplified, leading to experimentally resolvable changes in quasiparticle properties and spectral response. Our results establish a concrete sensitivity-based route to low-energy quantum-gravity phenomenology in a well-defined many-body platform and delimit the validity of the effective description. Furthermore, we report experimental validation on the QRed superconducting quantum processor (BSC-CNS).

AI.tldr: Impurity many-body observables are sensitive to ultraviolet deformations, affecting spectral and Ramsey measurements in a quantum computing framework, with experimental validation on a superconducting quantum processor.
AI.motivation: To explore the effects of ultraviolet deformations on impurity many-body observables and their implications in low-energy quantum gravity phenomenology.
AI.method: Utilized a deformed polaron-molecule Hamiltonian while ensuring the infrared sector's preservation to study the impacts on observables in a controlled quantum computing environment.
AI.result: Identified significant sensitivity of observables in regimes near the polaron-molecule crossover, leading to detectably altered quasiparticle properties and spectral responses.
AI.conclusion: Results provide a sensitivity-based approach to quantum gravity studies in many-body systems, supported by experimental results from the QRed superconducting quantum processor.

title: Quantum Horizon: An evaluation of quantum computing as a threat to Bitcoin and Ethereum
comment: 21 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Reproducible model code, data, and figures: https://github.com/imgcode/quantum-horizon
summary: Quantum computing poses a real, broad-based, but bounded and substantially mitigable threat to Bitcoin and Ethereum. We separate the two quantum algorithms that public discussion routinely conflates: Shor's algorithm breaks the elliptic-curve signatures (ECDSA over secp256k1, BLS over BLS12-381) that authorize spending, whereas Grover's algorithm does not meaningfully threaten proof-of-work mining, which is protected by a merely quadratic speedup, fault-tolerant per-operation costs, a square-root parallelization wall, and difficulty adjustment. Folding hardware scaling, the falling resource requirement, a fault-tolerance readiness lag, and expert surveys into a single Monte-Carlo forecast yields a wide, bimodal arrival distribution for a cryptographically relevant quantum computer: about a one-in-six chance by 2035, near 30% by 2040, and about 60% by 2050. Exposure is concentrated and mostly migratable: of Bitcoin's roughly six million quantum-exposed coins only about 2.3 million are irreducibly at risk, while 50 to 65% of Ether sits at key-revealed accounts that can adopt post-quantum signatures. A timely migration beats even an optimistic 2035 machine, so the binding constraint is governance, not technology. A survey of the top twenty cryptocurrencies finds none fully post-quantum. Reproducible models accompany every quantitative claim.

AI.tldr: Quantum computing presents a mitigable threat to Bitcoin and Ethereum, primarily affecting elliptic-curve signatures while not significantly impacting mining. A forecast indicates a notable increase in quantum computer relevance by 2050, emphasizing governance for timely migration to post-quantum signatures.
AI.motivation: To assess the threat of quantum computing to blockchain technologies, particularly Bitcoin and Ethereum, and to clarify confusions around quantum algorithms.
AI.method: A Monte-Carlo forecasting approach combines various factors, including hardware scaling, resource requirements, and expert surveys, to predict the arrival distribution of cryptographically relevant quantum computers.
AI.result: Forecast indicates a 1/6 chance of a relevant quantum computer by 2035, 30% by 2040, and 60% by 2050. Bitcoin has 2.3 million coins at risk, while Ethereum is at greater risk due to many coins being in vulnerable accounts.
AI.conclusion: Timely migration to post-quantum signatures is crucial and more influenced by governance than technology. A review shows no cryptocurrencies are fully prepared for post-quantum challenges.

title: Physics-Informed Variational Quantum Classifier for Phase Detection in Strongly Correlated Matter
summary: The characterisation of quantum phases in strongly correlated systems is a crucial milestone for the deployment of quantum sensors. In this work, we present a Physics-Informed Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) designed to detect the topological phase transition between the Fermi polaron quasiparticle and the molecular bound state. Unlike conventional Machine Learning approaches, our quantum architecture is constructed via the Trotterised time-evolution of an effective Hamiltonian, ensuring that the learnable parameters correspond to interpretable physical quantities. We show that the VQC efficiently discovers the optimal interferometric protocol, specifically the evolution time and effective bath interactions required to maximise the visibility of Ramsey fringes, thereby clearly distinguishing the Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) and Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) regimes. Furthermore, we report the validation of this classifier on the QRed superconducting quantum processor (BSC-CNS). Despite the intrinsic hardware noise and decoherence, the VQC preserves the relative ordering of the topological phases. We demonstrate that the physics-informed architecture achieves a linear gate complexity $\mathcal{O}(N)$, bypassing the exponential memory wall of classical simulation and ensuring scalability to many-body regimes.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a Physics-Informed Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) to detect topological phase transitions in strongly correlated quantum systems, showcasing its effectiveness in distinguishing BEC and BCS regimes through optimized interferometric protocols, validated on a superconducting quantum processor.
AI.motivation: Characterizing quantum phases in correlated systems is vital for advancing quantum sensors.
AI.method: A Physics-Informed Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) uses Trotterised time-evolution of an effective Hamiltonian to learn interpretable physical parameters, optimizing interferometric protocol for phase distinction.
AI.result: The VQC effectively identifies the Fermi polaron and molecular bound states, distinguishes BEC and BCS regimes, and maintains phase order despite hardware noise.
AI.conclusion: The architecture demonstrates favorable linear complexity $	ext{O}(N)$, offering scalability for many-body regimes while overcoming limitations of classical simulations.

title: Quantum gates with parametrically driven multi-qubit couplers
summary: Superconducting quantum processors could significantly profit from enhanced connectivity together with precise control of interactions and gates between qubits. Here we investigate plaquettes of four qubits that are coupled via a central tunable coupling circuit, so that not only gates between qubits connected by an edge of the plaquette can be executed but also between qubits across the diagonal. By numerically and analytically analyzing parametrically driven processes, we explore $\sqrt{\text{iSWAP}}$-gates between any pair of qubits, also across the diagonal, as well as three-qubit interactions and gates. For experimentally available circuit parameters, we for example find $\sqrt{\text{iSWAP}}$-gates with a gate time of 50 ns and 99.9\% fidelity, which is decreased to 99.4\% if two such gates are executed in parallel on disjoint qubit pairs in the plaquette. For three-qubit gates we find fidelities of 95\% fidelity at a gate time of 200 ns.

AI.tldr: This paper explores enhancing interactions and gate operations among qubits in superconducting quantum processors using four-qubit plaquettes with tunable coupling.
AI.motivation: To improve connectivity and precise control in superconducting quantum processors for better performance and fidelity in qubit interactions.
AI.method: Numerical and analytical analysis of parametrically driven processes to execute $	ext{iSWAP}$-gates and three-qubit gates in a four-qubit architecture.
AI.result: Achieved $	ext{iSWAP}$-gates with a gate time of 50 ns and 99.9% fidelity, slightly reduced to 99.4% for parallel operations; three-qubit gates show 95% fidelity at 200 ns.
AI.conclusion: Enhanced qubit connectivity enables high-fidelity gate operations, crucial for advancing superconducting quantum processors.

title: Dissipation-induced superradiance in matter coupled to a self-interacting cavity
comment: 6 pages main text, including references; 7 pages supplemental material, including references
summary: Light-matter interactions are often modeled via the Dicke model, namely, by two-level systems coupled to a cavity mode. Alas, the threshold for superradiance is often experimentally inaccessible or hindered by light's diamagnetic term. Here, within the Dicke setting, we consider self-interacting light in a cavity, modeled by a photonic Kerr nonlinearity. We show that negative Kerr nonlinearity gives rise to a low-threshold superradiant phase with spin inversion. While unstable in a closed system, cavity dissipation stabilizes this lit phase, opening avenues for lasing and bath-engineered phases.

AI.tldr: The paper explores the Dicke model of light-matter interactions, introducing self-interacting light through negative Kerr nonlinearity to achieve a low-threshold superradiant phase, stabilized by cavity dissipation.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the challenges of accessing the superradiance threshold in traditional light-matter models due to limitations imposed by experimental conditions and diamagnetic effects.
AI.method: The authors investigate the effects of negative Kerr nonlinearity on a two-level system coupled to a cavity, examining how this nonlinearity influences superradiant behavior when combined with cavity dissipation.
AI.result: The study finds that negative Kerr nonlinearity leads to a stable superradiant phase characterized by spin inversion, despite being unstable in isolated systems.
AI.conclusion: This work suggests that cavity dissipation can stabilize unusual quantum phases, potentially paving the way for new lasing mechanisms and engineered quantum states.

title: Scaling native entanglement generation in layered semiconductors with quasi-phase matching
summary: Efficient generation of entangled photons typically relies on spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) in phase-matched macroscopic nonlinear media. However, generating entanglement under phase-matching constraints requires additional bulk optics or interferometers. In contrast, ultrathin van der Waals semiconductors - such as transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) - exhibit strong enough optical nonlinearities for SPDC to be observed from subwavelength-thick media, thereby bypassing conventional phase-matching constraints. In this microscopic domain, the intrinsic crystal symmetry governs the nonlinear optical response, enabling the native generation of polarization-entangled photon pairs. However, generating these states efficiently has been fundamentally restricted by the material's coherence length ($L_c$), which limits the attainable conversion efficiency. Here, we investigate periodically-poled TMDs (PPTMDs) designed to scale up this interaction via quasi-phase matching. We demonstrate that mechanically flipping the sign of the nonlinearity at precise intervals of $L_c$ introduces quasi-phase matching, that scales the pair-production rate while preserving the pristine, symmetry-generated polarization entanglement, with fidelities exceeding 99%. Backed by a rigorous theoretical model, our work clarifies the interplay between crystal symmetry and propagation effects in thin nonlinear media, providing a new avenue for engineering quantum light in nanophotonic systems.

AI.tldr: This study presents a method to efficiently generate polarization-entangled photon pairs using periodically-poled transition metal dichalcogenides (PPTMDs), overcoming traditional phase-matching limitations and achieving high fidelity.
AI.motivation: To address the limitations in generating entangled photon states due to bulk optics and phase-matching constraints in conventional materials.
AI.method: The authors design periodically-poled TMDs to implement quasi-phase matching by mechanically flipping the sign of nonlinearity at specific intervals, enhancing pair-production rates while maintaining high-fidelity entanglement.
AI.result: The proposed method achieved polarization-entangled photon pairs with fidelities exceeding 99%, demonstrating a significant improvement in conversion efficiency.
AI.conclusion: This work highlights the relationship between crystal symmetry and nonlinear optical response, offering new pathways for quantum light engineering in nanoscale photonic systems.

title: On-site interactions in quantum thermal machines: efficiency, rectification and entanglement beyond local and global master equations
comment: Salvatore Araceli and Teddy H. M. Ong contributed equally to this work. 25 pages, 13 figures
summary: Advances in experimental techniques have opened new routes for harnessing non-equilibrium dynamics in mesoscopic quantum systems. In this context, we study the impact of on-site interactions on the transport properties of a continuous quantum thermal machine composed of two coupled oscillators connected to two thermal reservoirs. In the weak system-reservoir coupling regime, where a long-standing debate concerns which reduced description should be preferred, we first show that the Redfield master equation (RME) provides an accurate and unifying framework that interpolates between two well-known limits: the \textit{local} and \textit{global} master equations. By relying on the Hierarchy of Pure States (HOPS), a numerically exact stochastic method, we then explore the full parameter space and show that interactions can be leveraged to tune the efficiency of the thermal machine at high temperatures (while leaving it essentially unchanged at low temperatures), induce non-reciprocal transport under asymmetric reservoir couplings, and generate steady-state entanglement within the junction. We derive expressions for system-bath correlators, such as heat and particle currents, consistently across different frameworks. Our work features on-site interactions to enhance the versatility of quantum thermodynamic junctions and clarifies the role of non-Markovianity and non-linearities in quantum transport.

AI.tldr: The paper explores how on-site interactions in mesoscopic quantum systems affect transport properties, particularly for a thermal machine with two coupled oscillators.
AI.motivation: To unify differing theoretical descriptions of quantum thermal machines in the weak coupling regime and understand the effects of on-site interactions on efficiency and entanglement.
AI.method: Utilizing the Redfield master equation (RME) and the Hierarchy of Pure States (HOPS) approach, the authors investigate the full parameter space and derive expressions for system-bath correlators.
AI.result: Interactions are shown to enhance efficiency at high temperatures, create non-reciprocal transport with asymmetric couplings, and generate steady-state entanglement, clarifying the influence of non-Markovianity in quantum transport.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates how on-site interactions increase the versatility of quantum thermodynamic junctions and contribute to a deeper understanding of quantum transport dynamics.

title: No classical particle limit for massless quanta
summary: We investigate whether relativistic massless classical particles may emerge as the classical limit of massless quanta. To address this question independently of any specific dynamics, environment, or pointer basis, we develop an axiomatic and purely kinematical framework for the coarse-graining approach. In this formulation, a candidate classical phase space is taken as the outcome space of a POVM subject only to minimal classicality and covariance under the relevant spacetime symmetry group. Applying this framework to the Poincaré group, we prove a no-go theorem for massless particles: the covariance requirement is incompatible with the operational conditions for classicality. The theorem leaves open field-like limits of massless quanta, for example the emergence of electromagnetic or gravitational fields, while ruling out classical massless particles, such as classical photons or gravitons.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that relativistic massless classical particles cannot emerge from massless quanta under the set conditions, while allowing for the possibility of field-like limits.
AI.motivation: To determine if classical massless particles can arise as a classical limit of massless quanta in a general framework.
AI.method: An axiomatic kinematical framework for coarse-graining was developed, applying it to the Poincaré group to analyze classicality and covariance.
AI.result: A no-go theorem was proven, indicating that the covariance condition contradicts the operational requirements for classical massless particles.
AI.conclusion: While classical massless particles like photons or gravitons cannot exist under the established conditions, the emergence of field-like constructs such as electromagnetic or gravitational fields remains possible.

title: Quasilinear Equivalence Checking for Detector Error Models
summary:
A Detector Error Model (DEM) is a structured representation of error mechanisms in quantum circuits, which has gained popularity in quantum compilation pipelines for its ability to capture fault-tolerance at a circuit level. It lists error mechanisms as instructions targeting detectors and observables, specifying for each physical fault channel the probability that the fault fires, the detectors it triggers, and the observables it flips.
  In this paper, we develop an equational theory for DEMs, with its associated categorical semantics. We present a sound, terminating, confluent rewriting system for DEM terms, formulating it as a symmetric monoidal theory (a PROP) over the Giry monad. We prove that every DEM term has a unique normal form, which can be computed efficiently in quasilinear time $O(k|E|\log|E|)$, where $|E|$ is the number of instructions and $k$ bounds the size of a target set. This provides a complete set of invariants (via Tanner graphs) for structural DEM equivalence. We provide the first static decision procedure for DEM equivalence, with rigorous correctness guarantees. It is complete (decides full decoder-equivalence exactly) for non-adaptive quantum error correction (QEC) pipelines, and scales to a sound and applicable decision procedure for partially-adaptive circuits (lattice surgery, distributed QEC, ...) without suffering exponential overhead. We discuss its application to the verification and optimisation of quantum compilers.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an equational theory and a rewriting system for Detector Error Models (DEMs) in quantum circuits, enabling efficient normal form computation and static decision procedures for error equivalence in quantum error correction.
AI.motivation: To enhance understanding and manage the error mechanisms in quantum circuits, particularly for improving fault tolerance in quantum compilation.
AI.method: Development of an equational theory for DEMs and a symmetric monoidal theory over the Giry monad, leading to a sound and confluent rewriting system for efficient computation of normal forms.
AI.result: Establishment of unique normal forms for DEM terms, scalable decision procedures for error equivalence in quantum error correction, and guarantees for both non-adaptive and partially-adaptive circuits.
AI.conclusion: The methodology significantly aids in verifying and optimizing quantum compilers, showcasing the practical implications of the theoretical advancements.

title: Resolving the Edge of a Quantum Pyramid
summary: Standing on the shoulders of giants, we resolve the quantum pyramids conjecture, confirming the globally information-optimal measurement for an ensemble of equiangular equiprobable pure states, as conjectured by Englert and Řeháček (arXiv:0905.0510). We do so by proving the remaining entropy inequalities of Holevo and Utkin (arXiv:2506.06700), which certify optimality for obtuse and flat pyramids. For obtuse pyramids, our key contribution is a rigorous proof that local minimizers of the corresponding entropy inequality cannot have three distinct coordinate values. We show that eliminating this family can be reduced to a neat algebraic reciprocal inequality relating branches of the Lambert $W$ function, which may be of independent interest. For flat pyramids, we prove a tight $\ell^p$ inequality for zero-sum vectors that was recently conjectured, proved analytically in dimension $d=3$, and computationally verified for $d\leq 200$ by Holevo and Utkin (arXiv:2603.24017). We prove this bound for all $d\geq 2$ via a technique in symmetric inequalities known as the equal variables method.

AI.tldr: The paper resolves the quantum pyramids conjecture and confirms optimal measurements for equiangular equiprobable pure states by proving entropy inequalities for obtuse and flat pyramids.
AI.motivation: To address the quantum pyramids conjecture and establish the optimality of measurements conjectured by Englert and Řeháček.
AI.method: The authors prove remaining entropy inequalities using techniques from algebraic inequalities and symmetric inequalities, specifically focusing on local minimizers and the equal variables method.
AI.result: They provide a rigorous proof that local minimizers cannot have three distinct coordinate values for obtuse pyramids, and establish a tight $ p$ inequality for flat pyramids valid for all dimensions $d\geq 2$.
AI.conclusion: The findings confirm the conjectures related to quantum measurements and provide new insights into algebraic inequalities related to the Lambert $W$ function.
